definitions: The growth of a person , animal , or plant is its process of increasing in size :
an increase in the size or the importance of something:
a lump (= a solid mass ) growing on the outside or inside of a person , animal , or plant that is caused by a disease :
something that has grown :
the process of developing or of increasing in size :
examples: A balanced diet is essential for healthy growth.
Plant growth is most noticeable in spring and early summer .
The government is trying to limit population growth.
The rapid growth of opposition to the plan has surprised the mayor .
Electronic publishing is a growth area (= an area of activity that is increasing in size and developing quickly )
a cancerous growth on the liver

definitions: present participle of get
the group of people who officially control a country :
the system used for controlling a country , city , or group of people :
the activities involved in controlling a country , city , group of people , etc.:
the government of the UK:
the offices , departments , and groups of people that control a country , state , city , or other political unit :
examples: the government of Israel
The government is/are expected to announce its / their tax proposals today.
The minister has announced that there will be no change in government policy .
Senior government officials will be attending a meeting tomorrow .
Theatre companies are very concerned about cuts in government grants to the arts .
A government enquiry has been launched .

definitions: used before names of some cities to refer to both the city itself and the area around it:
examples: Greater Manchester
Greater Houston

definitions: increasing in size or quantity :
increasing in size or amount :
examples: There is a growing awareness of the seriousness of this disease .
A growing boy needs his food .
There is a growing awareness of the importance of recycling .
We have had to hire five more employees to meet growing demand .

definitions: an area on a playing field , that usually has two posts with a net fixed behind them, where players try to send the ball in order to score in sports such as football and hockey :
a point scored in some sports , such as football and hockey , when a player gets the ball into this area :
to be the player who tries to prevent the other team from scoring goals:
a goal area that has been left without any defenders :
an aim or purpose :
examples: Black headed the ball into the goal.
She won the ball and ran towards the goal.
Brazil won by three goals to one.
Only one goal was scored in the entire match .
Who is playing in goal for Milan this evening ?
He used to keep goal for Wimbledon.

definitions: belonging or relating to genes (= parts of the DNA in cells ) received by each animal or plant from its parents :
relating to the biological process by which the characteristics of living things are passed from parents to children
examples: a genetic defect / disease
genetically engineered plants

definitions: relating to the whole world :
considering or relating to all parts of a situation or subject :
including or affecting the whole world :
to start operating in countries all over the world :
examples: a global catastrophe / problem
This report gives a global picture of the company's finances .
We hope an era of peace and global cooperation has begun .
The company is trying to compete globally.
The President argued that technology and his energy plans "will help us to confront the serious challenge of global climate change ."
The firm made its bid to go global by taking over a leading American electronics distributor .

definitions: a group of people in a society who share particular qualities or ways of behaving which that society associates with being male , female , or another identity :
the condition of being a member of a group of people in a society who share particular qualities or ways of behaving which that society associates with being male , female , or another identity :
used to refer to the condition of being physically male , female , or intersex (= having a body that has both male and female characteristics ) :
the grammatical arrangement of nouns , pronouns and adjectives into masculine , feminine , and neuter types in some languages
to give someone or something a particular gender , or to think of something as belonging to a particular gender:
examples: I think all genders are able to care for children equally .
Those old films are full of racial and gender stereotypes .
Their goal is to eliminate gender bias in access to sports for children .
Germany's top court has ruled that parliament must legally recognize a third gender.
Our lab is committed to gender equality in the sciences and promotes men and women to senior positions in equal numbers .
"The gender that you identify with isn't always the same as your biological sex ," he explained .

definitions: a part of the DNA in a cell that controls the physical development , behaviour , etc. of an individual plant or animal and is passed on from its parents :
a specific chemical pattern on a chromosome (= cell structure ) that is received from the parents and controls the development of particular characteristics in an animal or plant
examples: The illness is believed to be caused by a defective gene.

definitions: a number of people or things that are put together or considered as a unit :
a number of people who play music together, especially pop music :
a business that contains several different companies :
a number of football teams who play each other in a competition . The winners of the group move onto the next stage of the competion :
the first part of a football competition in which teams are divided into groups and play only the other teams in their group. The winners of each group move onto the next stage of the competition :
examples: I'm meeting a group of friends for dinner tonight .
The car was parked near a small group of trees .
She showed me another group of pictures , this time of children playing .
What's your favourite group?
a pop / rock group
United News Media, the national newspaper and television group

definitions: past participle of give
knowing about or considering a particular thing:
already decided , arranged , or agreed :
to do something regularly or as a habit :
something that is certain to happen :
examples: Given his age , he's a remarkably fast runner .
The baby was looking very healthy , given that it was born prematurely .
Given the fact that he's had six months to do this, he hasn't made much progress .
At the given signal , the group rushed forward to the barrier .
The bomb could go off at any given (= any)
She was given to staying in bed till lunchtime .

definitions: considering the whole of someone or something, and not just a particular part of him, her, or it:
usually, or in most situations :
by most people , or to most people :
in a way that includes most people , things, or conditions , or most of the time :
examples: Your health is generally good, but you do have a few minor problems .
He wants more money to be given to the arts generally.
I shall now develop my previous point more generally (= to say more about what it includes )
The baby generally wakes up three times during the night .
Well, generally speaking (= in most situations )
It was generally believed at the time that both men were guilty .

definitions: to increase in size or amount , or to become more advanced or developed :
If your hair or nails grow, or if you grow them, they become longer :
If a plant grows in a particular place , it exists and develops there:
If you grow a plant , you put it in the ground and take care of it, usually in order to sell it:
to make a business bigger by increasing sales , employing more people , etc.:
examples: Children grow so quickly .
This plant grows best in the shade .
She's grown three centimetres this year .
Football's popularity continues to grow.
The labour force is expected to grow by two percent next year .
The male deer grows large , branching horns called antlers .

definitions: information intended to advise people on how something should be done or what something should be:
a piece of information that suggests how something should be done:
examples: The EU has issued guidelines on appropriate levels of pay for part-time manual workers .
The article gives guidelines on how to invest your money safely .
issue a guideline The EU has issued guidelines on appropriate levels of pay for part-time manual workers .

definitions: the act of giving money or other things to someone to help them or as a present :
the act of giving something such as information , advice , a message , etc.:
kind and willing to give help , emotional support , money , or other things:
the act of providing money for something, especially to a charity or other good cause :
examples: The government introduced new tax deductions to boost charitable giving.
He believes the internet has untapped potential for philanthropic giving.
Gift giving is not what Hanukkah is really about.
Recently, the giving of business gifts has declined .
The Official Secrets Act forbids the giving of any information in connection with her duties .
Our core area of business is the giving of investment advice .

definitions: involving or relating to most or all people , things, or places , especially when these are considered as a unit :
usually, or in most situations :
considering the whole of someone or something, and not just a particular part of him, her, or it:
to be a good thing for the public :
not detailed , but including the most basic or necessary information :
examples: The general feeling is that justice was not served .
There is general concern about rising crime rates .
My general impression of the place was good.
The talk is intended to be of general interest (= of interest to most people )
Rain will become more general in the southeast during the afternoon .
In general, men are taller than women.

definitions: organized sports activities that children do at school :
an organized competition consisting of several different sports events :
an organized competition consisting of different sporting events :
examples: the games teacher
It's games this afternoon .
I used to love games.
After maths , it's games.
His father was a games teacher and his mother was a nurse .
I couldn't do games because my ankle was so painful .
